task.description: Root-cause diagnosis of ISS-0515 (CI backend gate failing reproducibly on feature/WF02-REQ226-20260906 with cascading 200+-failure-per-partition data-integrity errors). CONFIRM OR REFUTE ORCH's advisory-lock/15s-timeout hypothesis with direct evidence, then hand off to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design (diagnosis only, no fix implemented).

result.note:
HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED, AND MECHANISM REFINED, BY DIRECT REPRODUCTION (not inference from CI logs alone). Full evidence trail below.

=== 1. Config confirmation (docs/issues/ISS-0515.yaml claim #2) ===
config/test.exs's `config :letflow, Letflow.Repo, ...` sets no `:timeout` key. Ecto.Repo's own default (deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo.ex) is 15000ms, and this applies to every `Repo.query!/2` call including test/support/tenant_template.ex:97's bare `Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext($1))", [@advisory_lock_key])` -- it is NOT overridden anywhere. Confirmed: the 15000ms figure in the hypothesis is exactly right, not a guess.

=== 2. Read test/support/tenant_template.ex in full ===
ensure_template!/0 (lines 68-129): the advisory-lock acquisition (`Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_lock...")`, line 97) is a BARE call, OUTSIDE the try/after that wraps the build+unlock (lines 99-124). If this specific query raises, the exception propagates straight out of ensure_template!/0 uncaught -- no rescue, no retry (tenant_fixture.ex explicitly documents 'One shot: no retry, no polling' at its own line 277). So a canceled lock-acquisition query fails exactly the ONE calling test with an uncaught exception; it does not itself loop or re-attempt a build. The atomic build-then-rename design (staging schema, rename-as-last-step) is otherwise sound and does correctly prevent a half-built schema from ever being observed under the literal name.

=== 3. DB-per-partition topology (materially refines the hypothesis) ===
config/test.exs line 65: `database: "letflow_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}"` -- every test_parallel.sh partition runs against a SEPARATE Postgres database (letflow_test1, letflow_test2, ...), not a shared one. Postgres advisory locks (pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock) are scoped per-database, not cluster-wide. CONSEQUENCE: the race is NOT literally 'all N partitions' first tenant-fixture test' as ISS-0515's filed hypothesis states -- cross-partition contention on this lock is structurally impossible. The real race is bounded to WITHIN one partition's own connection pool: however many async test processes in THAT ONE partition's BEAM VM happen to call `ensure_template!/0` for the first time before persistent_term's `@built_marker_key` is set (that flag is node-global once set, so only the very first wave of concurrent first-callers is at risk). ExUnit's default async concurrency (schedulers_online()*2) makes a 2+-way collision at partition boot entirely plausible whenever 2+ test files/cases needing a tenant fixture start around the same instant.

=== 4. DIRECT REPRODUCTION (the decisive evidence) ===
Environment: this sandbox has DB connectivity (mix ecto.create works) though no docker-cli/psql access. Ran against the REAL local dev DB on this branch (which already includes REQ-226's migration).

4a. Solo from-scratch build timing (DROP SCHEMA tenant_template CASCADE, then `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!()` timed directly): **1884.9 ms** and, in a second run, **1781.7 ms / 1932.5 ms**. This REFUTES the 'REQ-226's extra migration pushes real build time over 15s' framing of the hypothesis -- the real build is ~1.8-1.9s on this branch (54 migrations replayed), nowhere near 15000ms, even generously assuming CI hardware is several times slower than this box.

4b. Concurrency reproduction: dropped tenant_template, then launched 5 concurrent `Task.async` callers of `ensure_template!/0` against the SAME database/pool (simulating 5 async tests in one partition all needing the fixture for the first time at once; pool_size here = schedulers_online()*2 = 16, so NOT a connection-pool-exhaustion effect). Result, reproduced twice:
  - 1 winner: succeeds in ~1.78-1.93s (builds + renames + unlocks correctly).
  - 4 losers: ALL FAIL at 15009-15017 ms with `Postgrex.Error: ERROR 57014 (query_canceled) canceling statement due to user request` -- this is a byte-for-byte match to ISS-0515's own filed Postgres-log signature. 100% reproduction rate (2/2 runs, 4/4 losers each run) on an otherwise idle machine, with a build that only takes ~1.8s. This directly confirms the timeout-cancellation mechanism, and shows it is NOT a narrow, timing-margin-dependent effect -- it is a robust, near-certain failure any time 2+ callers race for this lock in the same partition, independent of build duration or migration count.

4c. pg_stat_activity was polled every ~1.5s throughout run 4b. All 4 losing backends showed `state=active, wait_event_type=Lock, wait_event=advisory, query=SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext($1))` continuously from t=0.5s through t=14.5s -- i.e. they were STILL shown waiting on the lock more than 12 SECONDS AFTER the winner's own `pg_advisory_unlock` completed (winner unlocked at ~1.78s in). This is the surprising part: prompt release-to-grant did not visibly occur within the observation window inside the full ensure_template!/0 flow.

4d. Isolated control probe (no ensure_template!/0, no Sandbox.mode/2 calls, no build work -- just 1 holder + 4 waiters contending on the SAME literal advisory-lock idiom directly, holder releases after a fixed 2s sleep, waiters given a generous 30_000ms query timeout): all 4 waiters were granted the lock and completed within ~1.88s of the holder's release, i.e. promptly and correctly. This ISOLATES the anomaly in 4c: bare pg_advisory_lock hand-off across concurrent Postgres sessions works fine on its own. Something specific to being INSIDE ensure_template!/0's surrounding machinery -- the leading candidate is every concurrent caller ALSO independently calling `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` as its own first statement (ensure_template!/0 line 82) at nearly the same instant -- correlates with the waiters never being visibly granted the lock before the 15s cutoff, rather than a genuine Postgres-side advisory-lock starvation bug. This secondary mechanism is NOT fully isolated/confirmed (would need a repro with Sandbox.mode/2 calls added back into the otherwise-clean 4d probe) and is flagged for CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV to verify before finalizing a fix, rather than asserted as fact here.

=== 5. scripts/test_parallel.sh (partition count / pool sizing) ===
N is derived from nproc/getconf or TEST_PARALLEL_N (never hardcoded, by design -- req113). TEST_POOL_SIZE is computed as (usable connection budget)/N when not explicitly set, with a floor of TEST_MIN_POOL_SIZE (default 2). At higher N (observed N=4 in the failing CI run per ISS-0515's filing), each partition's own pool can be quite small, which would make even a small handful of concurrent first-callers proportionally more likely to collide, but per §3/§4 above this is a secondary amplifier, not the primary mechanism -- the primary mechanism reproduces even with pool_size=16 and zero cross-partition contention at all.

=== 6. Existing retry/timeout surface (per ISS-0515's ask) ===
No existing timeout override, retry, or backoff exists on the `Repo.query!` call at tenant_template.ex:97, or anywhere in ensure_template!/0's lock-acquisition path. `tenant_fixture.ex` (the sole caller) is explicitly documented as one-shot/no-retry (line 277) -- a deliberate design choice for its own reasons (a retry would observe a different, already-partially-torn-down state), so any fix should not casually add a retry loop over ensure_template!/0 itself without re-examining that rationale.

=== ROOT CAUSE (confirmed) ===
test/support/tenant_template.ex's `ensure_template!/0` serializes concurrent first-time template builds via a SESSION-level Postgres advisory lock acquired through a bare `Repo.query!/2` call that is subject to Ecto's default 15000ms client-side query timeout (never overridden in config/test.exs). Under realistic async-test concurrency within a single test_parallel.sh partition (bounded per-partition since each partition is a separate Postgres database), 2+ processes calling `ensure_template!/0` for the first time before the node-global persistent_term marker is set will race for this lock; losers reliably (100% in direct repro) hit the 15000ms client timeout and raise `Postgrex.Error: query_canceled ... canceling statement due to user request` -- an exact match to ISS-0515's CI signature -- crashing whichever test triggered them, with NO retry. REQ-226 is implicated not because its one extra migration meaningfully lengthens the real build (~1.8-1.9s total, confirmed directly, nowhere near 15s), but because it added a new test module (test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs, 472 new lines, itself provisioning tenants) that raises the number of concurrent first-callers contending for this lock at partition boot, tipping a previously-rare race into a reliably-triggered one. The observed cascade of 200+ per-partition failures beyond the directly-crashed tenant-fixture tests is consistent with, but not fully isolated as being caused by, the pre-existing (and separately-designed/accepted, see ISS-0113/ISS-0423) `Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto)`-stays-on-for-the-rest-of-the-partition behavior interacting badly with an aborted/canceled connection mid-race -- flagged in §4d above as needing confirmation, not asserted as proven.

=== RECOMMENDED FIX DIRECTION (not implemented -- routing to CODE-DESIGNER) ===
Do NOT just bump the timeout on that one query as a first instinct without further verification: §4c's finding (waiters not visibly granted the lock even ~12s after release, inside the full flow, versus a clean isolated hand-off in §4d) means it is not proven that a larger timeout alone reliably fixes this -- it may only widen the window before the same failure recurs, or it may fully resolve it if the Sandbox.mode/2-concurrency theory in §4d is right. CODE-DESIGNER should evaluate two candidate directions and is not limited to these:
  (a) STRUCTURAL fix (more robust, larger scope): eliminate the per-first-caller race entirely by pre-building tenant_template ONCE, serially, before any partition's async tests are scheduled to run at all (e.g. an ExUnit `test_helper.exs`-level `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!()` call executed before `ExUnit.start()`'s test discovery/dispatch begins, or an equivalent single-shot setup hook) -- this removes the race's precondition (multiple concurrent first-callers) rather than trying to survive it.
  (b) LOCAL fix (smaller scope, needs the §4d Sandbox.mode/2 interaction verified first): pass a much larger (or `:infinity`) `:timeout` option specifically to the `Repo.query!` call at tenant_template.ex:97, AND verify under a repro identical to §4b (concurrency inside the real ensure_template!/0 flow, not the isolated §4d probe) that waiters are then reliably granted the lock in a bounded, reasonable time rather than hanging indefinitely -- if §4d's Sandbox.mode/2 theory is confirmed as the actual blocker, a bigger timeout alone will not fix it and (a) or a Sandbox.mode/2-avoidance change becomes necessary instead.
Either direction should preserve tenant_fixture.ex's documented one-shot/no-retry contract at its own call site, and should not touch `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`'s production path (test-only file, as its own moduledoc requires).

All repro scripts were run via `mix run -e` against the real local dev DB; no test/production code was modified. `DROP SCHEMA tenant_template CASCADE` was run three times as pre-authorized for this diagnostic; the schema was left rebuilt/healthy after the final run (confirmed present with a full table set from the successful racer/holder runs). No committed files were changed.
